tasks.title: NEW packages/opencode/src/agent/behaviors.ts (D16 schema + defaults + validator) + inter-agent-communication.ts behavior_violation extension
tasks.description: Foundation: D16 behavior contract schema + defaults + violation validator + InterAgentCommunication schema extension. (A) NEW packages/opencode/src/agent/behaviors.ts: export top-level `ABORT_REASONS = ['spec_wrong','transient_tool_error','out_of_scope','context_full','approach_failed','user_question'] as const` (literal `as const` so type narrows). Export Schema unions: `BehaviorVersion = Schema.Literals(['subagent_v1','subagent_v2'])`, `DeliveryRequirement = Schema.Literals(['send_message_required','send_message_optional','no_delivery'])`, `TerminationRequirement = Schema.Literals(['self_close','spawner_close','either'])`, `ViolationKind = Schema.Literals(['missing_delivery','undeclared_failure_mode','invalid_termination','output_shape_mismatch'])`. Export `class BehaviorContract extends Schema.Class<BehaviorContract>('BehaviorContract')({ version: BehaviorVersion, delivery: DeliveryRequirement, termination: TerminationRequirement, declared_failure_modes: Schema.Array(Schema.String), expected_outputs: Schema.optional(Schema.Struct({ kind: Schema.Literals(['json_schema','free_text']), schema: Schema.optional(Schema.Unknown) })), exempt: Schema.optional(Schema.Boolean) }) {}`. Export `class BehaviorViolation extends Schema.Class<BehaviorViolation>('BehaviorViolation')({ kind: ViolationKind, detail: Schema.String }) {}`. Export concrete default contracts: `generalSubagentV1` (delivery: 'send_message_required', termination: 'self_close', declared_failure_modes: all 6 ABORT_REASONS), `generalSubagentV2` (forward-compat placeholder — delivery: 'send_message_required', termination: 'either', declared_failure_modes: all 6 + optional expected_outputs free_text), `exploreSubagentV1` (delivery: 'send_message_required', termination: 'self_close', declared_failure_modes: 5 reasons MINUS 'approach_failed' per WAVE.md item 2). Export `DEFAULT_CONTRACTS: Record<string, { default_version: BehaviorVersion; versions: Record<string, BehaviorContract> }>` keyed by agent_type 'general' (default_version 'subagent_v1', versions { subagent_v1, subagent_v2 }) and 'explore' (default_version 'subagent_v1', versions { subagent_v1 }). Export `resolveContract = (agent_type?: string, version?: string): BehaviorContract | undefined` that returns undefined when agent_type is undefined / unknown, otherwise looks up DEFAULT_CONTRACTS[agent_type] and returns either the named version or the default_version. Export `computeViolations = (contract: BehaviorContract | undefined, observed: { delivered: boolean; abortReason?: { reason: string; details: string } }): BehaviorViolation[]` with logic: if contract undefined OR contract.exempt → return []; if delivery==='send_message_required' AND !observed.delivered → push { kind: 'missing_delivery', detail: 'child did not send_message/followup_task to spawner' }; if observed.abortReason AND !contract.declared_failure_modes.includes(observed.abortReason.reason) → push { kind: 'undeclared_failure_mode', detail: `abort_reason '${reason}' not in declared_failure_modes` }; return violations. Self-reexport `export * as Behaviors from './behaviors'`. Caveman-rich JSDoc throughout per codemaxxxing voice. (B) NEW packages/opencode/src/agent/behaviors.test.ts: >= 18 tests across these describe blocks: 'BehaviorContract schema' (decode happy path, decode rejects unknown version, decode preserves exempt + expected_outputs), 'BehaviorViolation schema' (decode happy + rejects unknown kind), 'DEFAULT_CONTRACTS structure' (general has v1 + v2, explore has v1 only, general default_version is subagent_v1, explore default_version is subagent_v1, explore v1 declared_failure_modes excludes approach_failed AND has 5 reasons, general v1 declared_failure_modes has all 6), 'resolveContract' (undefined agent_type → undefined, unknown agent_type → undefined, known agent_type without version → default_version contract, known agent_type with explicit version → that version's contract, known agent_type with unknown version → undefined), 'computeViolations' (no contract → empty, exempt contract → empty, send_message_required + delivered=false → missing_delivery, send_message_required + delivered=true → empty, send_message_optional + delivered=false → empty, undeclared abortReason → undeclared_failure_mode, declared abortReason → empty, combined: missing_delivery + undeclared_failure_mode), 'ABORT_REASONS constant' (exactly 6 entries in canonical order). Use describe + test (not it.live) since behaviors.ts is pure — no Effect runtime needed. Use Schema.decodeUnknownSync + Result for failure cases. 100% line coverage on behaviors.ts is mandatory (single-file run per GOTCHA bun-test-coverage-source-file-arg-runs-zero-tests). Function coverage may drift to ~95% because BehaviorContract / BehaviorViolation extend Schema.Class (per GOTCHA schema-class-function-coverage) — Lines=100.00 is the assertion. (C) MODIFY packages/opencode/src/agent/inter-agent-communication.ts: ADD `behavior_violation: Schema.optional(Schema.Struct({ contract_version: Schema.String, violations: Schema.Array(Schema.Struct({ kind: Schema.String, detail: Schema.String })) }))` field AFTER the abort_reason field. JSDoc block explaining D16 + machine-readability (separate from D5 prose warning); per WAVE.md gotcha 4 cross-reference. (D) MODIFY packages/opencode/src/agent/inter-agent-communication.test.ts: ADD tests in the existing describe blocks: 'construction' gets +1 test ('optional behavior_violation struct preserved when supplied (D16 Wave 8)'), 'schema validation' gets +1 ('decodes payload carrying behavior_violation'), 'JSON roundtrip' gets +1 ('preserves behavior_violation through JSON roundtrip'). Mirror the abort_reason test shape verbatim — same wording style, same assertions pattern (decode + read .behavior_violation?.contract_version, .behavior_violation?.violations[0].kind etc). Per-file 100% line coverage on inter-agent-communication.ts via single-file run.

tasks.title: agent.ts attaches behavior contracts to native agent_type records + exports behaviorContractFor helper
tasks.description: Per-agent_type registration: agent.ts imports Behaviors and attaches each native agent_type's behavior contract registry. (A) MODIFY packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts: ADD import `import { Behaviors } from './behaviors'` near the existing prompt imports. In the `agents` map definitions, attach behaviors to `general` and `explore` via the options field (which is `Record<string, Unknown>` per Info schema, so this requires NO schema change). For `general.options` swap from `{}` to `{ behaviors: Behaviors.DEFAULT_CONTRACTS['general'] }`. For `explore.options` swap from `{}` to `{ behaviors: Behaviors.DEFAULT_CONTRACTS['explore'] }`. Add a documentation comment immediately above both attachments referencing D16 + the multi-agent-subagent.txt 'Your behavior contract' section. ADD exported helper `export const behaviorContractFor = (agent_type: string | undefined, version?: string) => Behaviors.resolveContract(agent_type, version)` at the bottom of the file, before the self-reexport. This proxy gives non-Agent.Service consumers (e.g. control.ts) a stable surface for resolving the per-agent_type contract that respects future agent.ts wiring (today it's a straight passthrough; future iterations could inspect user config overrides via Agent.Service). Place the helper above `export * as Agent from './agent'` so it is re-exported via the Agent namespace. (B) DO NOT touch other agent records (build / plan / compaction / title / summary) — only native subagent types (general / explore) get behavior contracts per WAVE.md item 2. (C) DO NOT add per-spawn validation in agent.ts — that lives in control.ts (T3). agent.ts is the REGISTRATION surface; control.ts is the ENFORCEMENT surface. (D) No new test file is added in this task — agent.ts has no existing dedicated test file (only integration tests via Agent.defaultLayer). The new lines (1 import + 2 attachments + 1 export + comment blocks) are trivially covered by every integration test that loads Agent.defaultLayer (every multi-agent-invariants.test.ts test, every agent-* tool test, etc.). Verification asserts the new lines exist via grep + that existing tests still pass + that typecheck stays clean. No coverage assertion on agent.ts as a whole (pre-existing baseline acknowledged per Wave 6/7 precedent for files without dedicated test files).

tasks.title: control.ts D16 runtime validation: behaviorOf per-root storage + SpawnAgentInput.behavior_version + completion-watcher behavior_violation attachment + D16 control.test.ts describe block
tasks.description: Runtime validation at terminal-status time. (A) MODIFY packages/opencode/src/agent/control.ts: import `import { Behaviors, BehaviorContract } from './behaviors'` (the Behaviors namespace re-export AND the BehaviorContract type for the map). Extend `SpawnAgentInput` with `readonly behavior_version?: 'subagent_v1' | 'subagent_v2'` (optional union literal; D16 doc comment block explaining default lookup via agent_type). Extend `PerRootData` with `readonly behaviorOf: Map<SessionID, BehaviorContract>` initialized in `ensureRootSlot` (alongside `links`/`linkedDeathOf` from Wave 7); cleared in BOTH the Session.Event.Deleted subscriber AND the disposal finalizer (>=2 .clear() call sites per the existing convention for every PerRootData map). In `spawnAgent`'s success branch (after `slot.statuses.set(child.id, status)` and BEFORE the completion-watcher fork), resolve the contract via `const contract = Behaviors.resolveContract(input.agent_type, input.behavior_version); if (contract) slot.behaviorOf.set(child.id, contract)`. Store the contract under the CHILD's session id (not the parent). The resolveContract call MUST NOT fail or throw — `Behaviors.resolveContract` returns undefined for any unknown agent_type, no contract is stored, no validation fires (which is the correct behavior for unregistered agent_types per WAVE.md gotcha 1). In the completion-watcher, AFTER the abort_reason parse (line ~1193) and AFTER `effectiveAbortReason` is computed but BEFORE constructing the InterAgentCommunication for the parent notification, compute the behavior_violation payload: `const contract = slot.behaviorOf.get(child.id)`; `const violations = Behaviors.computeViolations(contract, { delivered: childDelivered, abortReason: effectiveAbortReason })`; `const behavior_violation = contract && violations.length > 0 ? { contract_version: contract.version, violations: violations.map((v) => ({ kind: v.kind, detail: v.detail })) } : undefined`. Pass `behavior_violation` as the new optional field on the InterAgentCommunication constructor call (the watcher's `sendInterAgentCommunication` call). D16 inline doc comment block explaining the additive nature + relationship to D5 safety net (both can fire on the same case; D5 is prose, D16 is machine-readable). (B) MODIFY packages/opencode/src/agent/control.test.ts: ADD new `describe('AgentControl D16 behavior contract validation', () => { ... })` block AFTER the existing D15 describe (after L4418). Use `provideTmpdirInstance` per the existing pattern. Required tests (>= 6 it.live tests inside the block): (1) 'no contract attached when agent_type is undefined' — spawnAgent without agent_type, child terminates, parent's notification carries NO behavior_violation field. (2) 'no contract attached when agent_type is unknown' — spawnAgent with agent_type 'foo_bar', child terminates, parent's notification carries NO behavior_violation. (3) 'general subagent with send_message_required + no delivery → missing_delivery violation' — spawnAgent with agent_type 'general', stub runLoop writes assistant message but does NOT call send_message, parent's notification has behavior_violation.contract_version='subagent_v1' AND violations[0].kind='missing_delivery'. (4) 'general subagent that delivers via sendInterAgentCommunication → no violation' — spawnAgent with agent_type 'general', stub runLoop calls control.sendInterAgentCommunication(parentID, msg-with-recipient=parent-path), terminates, parent's notification carries NO behavior_violation (or empty violations). (5) 'explore subagent emitting ABORT(approach_failed) → undeclared_failure_mode violation (explore declared modes exclude approach_failed)' — spawnAgent with agent_type 'explore', stub runLoop writes 'ABORT(approach_failed): tried 3x.' as last assistant line, parent's notification has behavior_violation.violations contains undeclared_failure_mode. (6) 'subagent_v2 declared via spawn behavior_version arg uses subagent_v2 contract — coexistence' — spawnAgent with agent_type 'general' AND behavior_version 'subagent_v2', notification's behavior_violation.contract_version (when fires) reads 'subagent_v2'. (7) 'spawn succeeds even when subsequent runtime violates contract — validation is observer-only (INV-D-26 unit)' — assert that spawnAgent returns LiveAgent normally even for the cases above (no spawnAgent failure). Use writeAssistantMessage helper duplicated from D5/D11/D12 block precedent (local to the new describe). Tests use REAL AgentControl + Behaviors; no mocks. Per-file 100% LINE coverage on control.ts via single-file run (function% may stay at pre-existing Schema.TaggedErrorClass baseline per GOTCHA — this task only needs LINES=100.00).

tasks.title: Prose updates: multi-agent-subagent.txt 'Your behavior contract' section + prose/subagent-prompts.test.ts assertions
tasks.description: Prose: declared per-agent_type behavior contracts are visible to the model. (A) MODIFY packages/opencode/src/agent/prompt/multi-agent-subagent.txt: ADD a new section `## Your behavior contract` placed AFTER the `## ABORT — structured failure exits` section (end of file). The section explains: (i) every subagent has a DECLARED behavior contract attached to its agent_type at spawn time; (ii) the contract names what delivery shape the supervisor expects (typically `send_message_required` — call send_message to your spawner OR your work is invisible), the termination mode (typically `self_close`), the set of declared failure modes (the canonical ABORT reasons appropriate for your agent_type — `general` accepts all six; `explore` accepts five excluding `approach_failed` because explore doesn't iterate on a rubric), and optionally the expected output shape; (iii) at terminal-status time the runtime validates your observed behavior against the declared contract and surfaces structured `behavior_violation` payloads to the supervisor — so violating the contract is OBSERVABLE, not invisible; (iv) the simple rule: deliver via send_message before close_agent, only emit ABORT reasons your agent_type declares, and you stay inside the contract; (v) pointer back to ## Delivery contract + ## ABORT sections for the operational details. Caveman voice — short fragments, no fluff. ~15-22 lines. (B) MODIFY packages/opencode/test/prose/subagent-prompts.test.ts: ADD new assertions: required-phrases — multi-agent-subagent.txt MUST contain substrings 'Your behavior contract' AND 'behavior_violation' AND 'declared failure modes' (or 'declared_failure_modes'). Forbidden-phrases unchanged. The new assertions land inside the existing describe block (or a new describe('multi-agent-subagent D16 behavior contract prose', () => { ... })). Do NOT touch any other prompt file (PROMPT_SURFACES.md ownership map: D16 prose lives in multi-agent-subagent.txt ONLY — root.txt does not own it because supervision/validation is observed by the SPAWNER which is typically root anyway; root's existing ## Sibling coordination + ## Limits sections are sufficient). Verification asserts the prose grep + that prose/subagent-prompts.test.ts passes.

tasks.title: INV-D-24..26 integration invariants: validate D16 end-to-end against the spec
tasks.description: Lock D16 behavior contracts via integration invariants. ADD three new it.instance blocks INSIDE the existing `describe('INTEGRATION_INVARIANTS — multi-agent surfaces')` block, AFTER the INV-D-23 block (around L2685). Tests MUST run RED against pre-T3 code and GREEN against post-T3 code. (1) `INV-D-24-agent-type-behavior-contract-validated-at-spawn` — registerRunLoop drives a child that writes one assistant text (no send_message to spawner) then exits. Spawn /root/g24 with agent_type='general'. After ~80ms drainMailbox(root.id). Assert: parent's notification has author=/root/g24, content includes 'reached status:', AND behavior_violation IS present, behavior_violation.contract_version === 'subagent_v1', behavior_violation.violations.length >= 1, behavior_violation.violations[0].kind === 'missing_delivery'. The D5 safety-net prose warning may or may not be in content (depends on whether body looks like missing-deliverable text per existing logic) — the D16 assertion is ABOUT the structured payload field, which IS authoritative for INV-D-24. (2) `INV-D-25-behavior-contract-version-bump-coexists-with-prior-version` — Spawn TWO children under same root: one with agent_type='general' + behavior_version='subagent_v1' (named /root/v1child), one with agent_type='general' + behavior_version='subagent_v2' (named /root/v2child). Same stub runLoop writes assistant text + ABORT(spec_wrong) for both (both emit a declared ABORT reason that's in BOTH v1 and v2 declared_failure_modes — to avoid the undeclared_failure_mode noise). After ~150ms drainMailbox. Assert: v1child's notification has behavior_violation.contract_version === 'subagent_v1'; v2child's notification has behavior_violation.contract_version === 'subagent_v2'. No cross-contamination (v1child does NOT carry subagent_v2 string). Both violations have missing_delivery kind (neither called send_message). (3) `INV-D-26-behavior-contract-violation-fails-orchestrated-wave-not-spawn` — assert spawn itself returns LiveAgent successfully even when the contract WILL be violated. Spawn /root/inv26 with agent_type='general'; LiveAgent returned has thread_id set + initial status non-final (no spawn-time error). Then drive runLoop that NEVER calls send_message + close (or completes silently). Within ~80ms parent's mailbox has the completion notification carrying behavior_violation — the SPAWN returned cleanly (no error wrapped in Effect.failure / Result.failure); the VIOLATION is observed AFTER spawn via the mailbox notification. Use Result wrappers + Result.isSuccess assertions on the spawn return. Comments on each test reference the WAVE.md gotcha (gotcha 1: validation at terminal time; gotcha 2: existing tests w/o agent_type continue to work — these tests intentionally pass agent_type to opt INTO validation; gotcha 4: D5+D16 relationship documented). Use the existing testEffect + Layer.mergeAll machinery + the shared registerRunLoop pattern at top of file. All three tests assert via real AgentControl + real Behaviors (no mocks).
